summary: Instagram is where almost all the audience is: most Hindi videos get roughly 1,000-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best performers are short, punchy 'X doesn't do what you think, it only does Y' explainers on relatable sensors and robots (clap switch, gyro robot, mic, DHT11). Question-style 'Kaise kaam karta hai? 🤔' titles and the October videos posted only on YouTube got almost no traction, and the newest videos (mid to late November) are weaker on Instagram, with the exception of the UV sensor one, which got many shares.
winningPattern: Instagram-first Hindi explainers about a familiar maker sensor or robot (clap switch, gyro, mic, DHT11, IR, line follower). Title hook is a myth-bust contrast: 'Yeh X nahi karta, sirf Y karta hai' or a dramatic consequence ('Gyro ke bina robot turant gir jaata'), with one emoji and #shorts. Saves come from build-it-yourself, Arduino-relevant topics, and shares come from surprising everyday facts (sunburn through clouds, soil sensor).
doMore: Post to Instagram Reels every time and treat YouTube as secondary; the October YouTube-only posts averaged very little
Use the myth-bust contrast hook ('doesn't see/hear/smell, only does X') on well-known sensors and robots
Build on the clap switch and robot winners with a series, such as part 2 or related fails, because those topics repeatedly pull 1,200-1,400 views
Pair a surprising everyday-life angle with a maker sensor (like UV through clouds) to drive shares, and add a build tip or wiring detail to drive saves
Open with the visual payoff or a dramatic failure in the first second, and end with a prompt such as 'save this for your project' or 'send to a friend who builds robots'
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai? 🤔' question titles with no surprise or contrast
Posting to YouTube only, or repeating near-duplicate topics (a fourth clap switch or PIR video) that split the audience
Niche, abstract topics like geophone, TDS meter, CO2 and geyser thermocouple without a relatable hook
